deep.reconstruction:
This page is part of the transfinite 'small object argument' in Grothendieck's stacks notes (the date is given as 'from 1982', so this may be the period of Pursuing Stacks). The ambient category M is locally presentable (topos-like). L_0 is a set of arrows. Ψ is the class of maps with the right lifting property with respect to L_0. L is the class of maps generated from L_0 by cobase change and by direct limits (transfinite composition), plus presumably retracts. These classes are defined on earlier pages, not shown here.

The goal is to factor an arbitrary f: X→Y as f = p∘i with i ∈ L and p ∈ Ψ. On previous pages a transfinite sequence X → X_α(f) → Y has been built. At each step one pushes out along all lifting problems from L_0, and at limit stages one takes direct limits.

The question settled on this page is when to stop the induction.
- A cardinal π_g is attached to each g ∈ L_0: the smallest cardinal such that the source and target of g are π-accessible.
- Example: if all these sources and targets are of finite presentation (Hom(A,−) commutes with filtered direct limits), then π = ω (or ℵ_0) and one stops at α_0 = the first infinite ordinal. This is Quillen's countable small object argument.
- In general the objects are only accessible. One takes π large enough that each Hom(A,−) commutes with direct limits indexed by ordinal sets that are 'large with respect to π'.
- α_0 is then the first ordinal whose initial segment I_{α_0} = {α < α_0} is large with respect to π. In effect this is a regular cardinal above π.
- One sets X(f) = X_{α_0}(f), i(f) = i_{α_0}(f), p(f) = p_{α_0}(f).

The hypotheses made explicit in (a) are:
- the sources and targets of the arrows of L_0 are accessible (automatic if M is a topos, etc.);
- π = sup(π_0, card L_0), where π_0 is the cardinality of the smallest α_0 such that every such Hom(A,−) commutes with direct limits of type I_{α_0};
- for filtering direct systems with index set of cardinality ≤ π and transition maps in L, the direct limit exists and the coprojections Z_i → Z lie in L. In other words, L is closed under transfinite composition of that size.

The conclusion is twofold:
- i(f) ∈ L and p(f) ∈ Ψ. Any lifting problem from some g ∈ L_0 against p(f) factors through some X_α, because Hom(source(g), −) commutes with the colimit over I_{α_0}. It is therefore solved at stage α+1.
- The factorization X(f) is functorial in f, because the construction is canonical (it uses all commutative squares). This is the functorial factorization needed for model-category structures, e.g. on categories of (pre)stacks or simplicial objects in a topos.
errors: Read literally, 'first ordinal α_0 such that I_{α_0} is large wrt π' is ambiguous. What is needed is that α_0 be a regular cardinal (cofinality > the presentability rank of the domains), e.g. the successor cardinal of π. Any ordinal of small cofinality would not work, however large its cardinality.

The hypothesis in (a) speaks of systems with index set of cardinality ≤ π, yet the construction runs up to α_0, which is of cardinality > π in general. So the size bound in the hypothesis seems off by one cardinal (it should be < α_0 or ≤ card α_0). Closure of L under arbitrary transfinite composition would avoid the issue.
Only Hom(A,−) commuting with colimits of chains of L-maps is actually needed (relative smallness). The stated hypothesis is stronger than necessary, but not wrong.
Existence of the necessary coproducts and pushouts in M (for the successor steps) is not restated here; presumably it is assumed earlier.

ideas.what: Transfinite small object argument: factorization f = p∘i with i in the saturation L of a set L_0 and p having the RLP with respect to L_0, stopping at a regular ordinal above the accessibility rank of the domains/codomains
ideas.modern_name: (Transfinite) small object argument; cofibrantly generated weak factorization systems
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quillen (1967, countable case); Gabriel–Ulmer (1971); Bousfield (1977); later Hovey, Hirschhorn, Beke, J. Smith (combinatorial model categories, ~1998–2000)
ideas.where_published: Transfinite constructions with accessible objects and cardinals appear in SGA 4 Exposé I §9 (possibly; uncertain). Model-category questions are discussed in Pursuing Stacks, but I am unsure whether this exact argument appears there.

ideas.what: Use of the accessibility rank of objects (smallest π such that Hom(A,−) commutes with π-filtered colimits) to bound the length of the induction; finite presentation as the ω case
ideas.modern_name: κ-presentable / κ-accessible objects; locally presentable categories

ideas.what: Functoriality of the factorization in f
ideas.modern_name: Functorial factorization (Quillen model structure axiom MC5, functorial version)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quillen; standard in Hovey 1999 and Hirschhorn 2003

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard version of the transfinite small object argument, with functorial factorization, in an accessible/topos setting. It is mathematically routine and well documented in later literature (Bousfield, Hovey, Beke, Smith). The only historical interest is that Grothendieck was writing out the general accessible-object version himself in the early-to-mid 1980s, roughly contemporaneous with or before its codification in model-category texts.

'we get π = ω [?]': the symbol is a heavily inked zero/omega; read as ℵ_0 or ω (first infinite ordinal), consistent with the next sentence.
'(still they are accessible)': the handwriting is 'still they are accessible', after a struck-through word.
Hypothesis a): 'π_0 is the cardinality of the smallest ordinal α_0 such that' (with α_0 written above).
